Who We Are № 02

About
Prep Up.

A non-profit closing the guidance gap between independent school college counseling and the public school students of the Southcoast.

Mission A statement of intent

Prep Up offers a high-touch, cohort-based college advisory program designed to close any "guidance gap."

By adapting the college counseling models of top independent schools for a community-based setting, we provide a scalable, multi-year architecture that can be tailored to meet students' needs and transform their potential into collegiate success.

Our approach is process-driven and developmentally grounded — meeting students where they are in 9th grade and walking alongside them through every step to enrollment.

Values What we stand for

Three principles
in everything we do.

01

Equity

A commitment to access and transparency. Every student deserves the same quality of guidance regardless of background or resources.

02

Partnership

A collaborative, process-driven method of support. We work alongside students and families, not just for them.

03

Aspiration

Setting the bar high for every student's future. We believe in possibilities, not just probabilities.

The Founders Meet the team

Two educators.
Sixty years of practice.

Prep Up was founded by two educators who spent decades giving students at elite independent schools something that should be available to everyone.

ST
Photo Forthcoming № 01

Founder · 01

Stuart Titus

Co-founder

Stuart has worked for over three decades at independent schools in the Northeast. He was the Director of College Counseling at Mercersburg Academy in Pennsylvania, and a counselor at Tabor Academy in MA and San Francisco University High School in CA. Stuart, who was a three-year letter winner on the football team at Bates College, was also a College Counselor, English teacher, football and tennis coach, and dorm parent at St. George's School in RI.

LJ
Photo Forthcoming № 02

Founder · 02

Lucia Jaccaci

Co-founder

Lucia is an educator with 30 years of experience in independent school education. She has worked both as a classroom teacher and an administrator in the United States and in China. She taught history at St. George's School in RI and Cincinnati Country Day School in OH. While at YK Pao School in Shanghai she helped develop the college counseling program. Upon moving to the Southcoast, Lucia taught citizenship classes at the Immigrant Assistance Center in New Bedford, and is currently volunteering at Our Sister's School and Damien's Food Pantry.
